summary: PASS. TASK-141 now has a usable generator-to-CARLA runtime surface with both local contract proof and live Kasm CARLA proof. The live manifest proves generated object/asset spawns and one generated behavior actor in CARLA with 450 RGB frames, 7,650 tracks, actor cleanup, a 90s MP4, and explicit `closed_loop_vla_control=false` and `real_time_vla_control=false` boundaries. The live score artifact now blocks only on intentional one-behavior breadth, not on a false missing-tracks blocker.

finding_log.summary: The live Kasm run is simulator proof, not the breadth-promotion run; its `generator_runtime_score=85.0000` is below threshold because it used one behavior case.
evidence: The fixed live score components are scenario_generation=15, behavior_breadth=7, object_spawn_readiness=18, carla_runtime_proof=20, cleanup_and_lineage=15, and claim_honesty=10.
The fixed live score blocker list is only `generator_runtime_score 85.0000 below 90.0000`; the earlier false `missing runtime entity tracks` blocker was removed by accepting case-result track paths.
The fake-CARLA breadth smoke still scores 98.0000 with three behavior cases, while the Kasm run proves actual CARLA spawning/video for one selected behavior.
finding_log.next_action: Use the Kasm live run as CARLA evidence and the fake-CARLA three-behavior run as breadth evidence; run a multi-behavior live Kasm batch only if the final judge packet needs the live metric to cross 90.

rubric_sections.name: code-quality
findings: `run_generated_scenario_runtime` dispatches cleanly across dry-run, fake-CARLA, and carla-live backends without top-level CARLA import.
The live backend reuses `run_carla_ood_demo` and writes a separate `generated_runtime_live_carla_proof.json`, keeping simulator side effects at the runtime edge.

The score module is small and transparent enough to diagnose why the live one-behavior proof scores 85 while the fake breadth proof scores 98, and it now accepts live case-result track paths when a top-level tracks path is absent.
rubric_sections.next_action: Future hardening should add a multi-behavior live batch wrapper rather than expanding the core runtime module much further.

rubric_sections.name: integration-readiness
findings: `oodrive generate-run` and `oodrive score-generator-runtime` are product CLI commands with focused tests and docs.
Local Mac absence of CARLA still produces a blocked manifest, while the Kasm RunPod path proves the same backend against a live CARLA server.
The manifest preserves claim labels for generated behavior/object runtime proof without inflating it into closed-loop VLA control.
rubric_sections.next_action: Hand TASK-139 the live runtime manifest/video for time-warped VLA stitching, keeping control claims false until Alpamayo outputs drive controls.

The live proof reports 450 RGB frames, 7,650 tracks, five static/generated object spawns, one dynamic behavior actor, and spawned actor cleanup.
The QA artifact maps fake-CARLA breadth proof, local blocked proof, live Kasm proof, fixed score output, ffprobe output, and command history to the acceptance criteria.
rubric_sections.next_action: No further TASK-141 evidence is blocking; the remaining improvement is optional live-breadth scoring if a later packet wants one live run to satisfy both simulator proof and metric threshold.

rubric_sections.name: video-quality

The clip is proof-friendly but not yet the final polished VLA-control story because it is a generated-runtime CARLA render without Alpamayo control stitched into the ego loop.
